lines.text: A toad's jewel was fish teeth.
For centuries, Europeans believed a jewel grew inside a toad's head.
Shakespeare wrote that the toad wears a jewel in his head.
From the 1300s, jewelers set these stones in rings.
lines.say: From the thirteen hundreds, jewelers set these stones in rings.

lines.text: Wearers thought the stone would sweat near poison.
It was also thought to cure kidney trouble and fits.
A museum label says the stones are fossil fish teeth.
They come from an extinct fish called Lepidotes.
lines.say: They come from an extinct fish called Leh pih doe teez.

lines.text: That fish swam in the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.
People in Europe still wore them as charms in the 1700s.
lines.say: People in Europe still wore them as charms in the seventeen hundreds.
